#### What this PR does / why we need it:

This fixes an upstream issue reported in Podman: https://github.com/containers/podman/issues/29633

Root cause : So the current logic, does not work becuase the architecture of the host get's updated incorrectly in the if-else block and it does not reset when `s.stages` > 1 becuase the architecture of the host is not null.
Subsequent builds assumes that we are running the image on different architecture which shouldn't be the case. 

So the solution should be simply decoupling the (if-else) a bit such that when we are on multi-satge builds it sepcifically distinguishes if we are using the `--platform` flag or not, if not then `s.stages` logic should always reset to the global build architecture that is null.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:
Fixes : https://github.com/containers/podman/issues/29633

Probably a better RN:
Fix multi-stage builds incorrectly forcing the host platform when a stage omits FROM --platform.
Ephemeral COPR build failed. @containers/packit-build please check.
@hihry, thoughts on my comment?  I'm not married to the change, but I would like you to consider it.  Plus, this needs a rebase now.

Actually the code changes that was suggested, were failing on the regression test `bats -f "build must reset platform" ./tests`, the stage context was getting leaked into later stages for that code, so we do need a reset branch which resets the context of the stages to the `host architecture`.

And the root cause for that is that when we first hit any stage with `--platform=arch64` then the libimage pulls that image into the storage and store it, when later stages hit the same image but without `--platform` flag, then that stage recieves fresh copeis of `systemContext` , which inturn sets `ArchitectureChoice to null`

The libimage does not interpret the `ArchitectureChoice` that is null to be that of the `host architecutre` and eventually pull that image that was stored in `container/storage` previously which is of incorrect architecture

@TomSweeneyRedHat , I have rebased the branch PTAL

> This PR is related to [podman-container-tools/podman#27779](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/27779). By no longer forcing the host platform on stages where no `--platform` was used, it eliminates the trigger for spurious registry pulls that overwrite local images in multi-stage builds. Instead of using `effectivePlatform = "local"` as a sentinel that relies on `parse.Platform("local")` internally calling `DefaultPlatform()`, the reset branch should copy the values directly from the executor's global `systemContext`, the same one that `startStage()` already copies per stage:
> 
> ```go
> s.systemContext.ArchitectureChoice = s.executor.systemContext.ArchitectureChoice
> s.systemContext.VariantChoice = s.executor.systemContext.VariantChoice
> s.systemContext.OSChoice = s.executor.systemContext.OSChoice
> ```
> 
> This correctly resets to the global build platform (from `buildah build --platform=X`) or to empty when none was given, letting libimage use its default lookup path without forcing a platform match. 

for global build platform, I have update the PR to use the `systemContext` from the executor block, but I think we do need the `effectivePlatform="local"`, because if there is no global build then `s.executor.systemContext.ArchitectureChoice = ""` which creates the same problem IMO, of pulling the incorrect architecture of that particular image from storage (failing the regression) ? 

if sentinel string is something that is not liked, then we can directly call `DefaultPlatform()` instead of using the sentinel string but that would be extra lines of code

Also added another test, even though the tests that I added seems identical in practice but these are two different case-scenarios that were faced.
